note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Stochastic-Power-HOOT: motivation, algorithm design, theory, and empirical results

nodes.name: MCTS limits in continuous stochastic settings
nodes.description: Real-world MCTS applications involve continuous actions and stochastic dynamics, where value estimates are non-stationary and actions cannot be enumerated, complicating both convergence theory and practice.

nodes.name: HOOT lacks guarantees
nodes.description: HOOT couples MCTS with the HOO hierarchical bandit but uses logarithmic exploration bonuses, which fail to guarantee convergence when value estimates are non-stationary because non-stationary rewards lack concentration.

nodes.name: POLY-HOOT is deterministic-only
nodes.description: POLY-HOOT adds a polynomial bonus and has non-asymptotic convergence guarantees in deterministic continuous MDPs, but no analogous guarantee exists for stochastic environments.

nodes.name: Stochastic-Power-HOOT
nodes.description: Stochastic-Power-HOOT is an MCTS algorithm for continuous-action stochastic MDPs that uses a power mean as value backup operator and a polynomial exploration bonus C n^(b/beta)/T_a(n)^(alpha/beta).

nodes.name: Power mean interpolates
nodes.description: The power mean f_n(p) interpolates between the arithmetic mean (p=1, conservative) and the maximum (p to infinity, optimistic), enabling tuning of exploration-exploitation across levels of stochasticity.

nodes.name: Enhanced HOO convergence
nodes.description: For non-stationary continuous-armed bandits satisfying the fixed-arm and optimal-arm convergence properties, an enhanced HOO agent with polynomial bonus achieves ||f_n - f||_inf at most C/n^zeta for some 0<zeta<1/2 (Theorem 1, Mao et al.).

nodes.name: Power mean preserves concentration
nodes.description: Power mean aggregation of estimators that concentrate polynomially preserves polynomial concentration at a transformed rate (Theorem 2).

nodes.name: Tree analysis by induction
nodes.description: Each internal MCTS node is modeled as a non-stationary bandit whose arms are child nodes; concentration rates are propagated inductively from rollout leaves at depth D upward using Q-value concentration (Lemma 1) and Theorem 2.

nodes.name: Polynomial convergence rate
nodes.description: Stochastic-Power-HOOT converges at rate O(n^-zeta), zeta in (0,1/2), where n is the number of visited trajectories, matching POLY-HOOT's rate while extending the guarantee to stochastic MDPs (Theorem 4).

nodes.name: Strong results on stochastic control
nodes.description: On stochastic classic control, all methods solve basic CartPole but only Stochastic-Power-HOOT handles CartPole with increased gravity optimally, with particular strength on sparse-reward MountainCar and high-gravity Acrobot (Table 2).

nodes.name: Scales to MuJoCo
nodes.description: On stochastic MuJoCo tasks it keeps strong performance in 17-dimensional Humanoid, achieving 3.1x the UCT baseline (Table 3).

nodes.name: Best power depends on environment
nodes.description: The optimal p varies by environment: Humanoid benefits from p=2 while the more stochastic Hopper needs p=8 (Table 3).

nodes.name: Moderate p works best
nodes.description: On CartPole-IG, p=2 and p=4 perform best: too low a p fails to focus search and too high may over-commit to early estimates (Table 4).

isolated_nodes.name: Environments are noisy variants
isolated_nodes.description: Experiments use stochastic versions of benchmarks with action noise, dynamics noise and observation noise (Gaussian perturbations), and rewards shifted to be strictly positive since power means require positive inputs.

structural_reasoning: The argument moves from the gap left by HOOT and POLY-HOOT to the power-mean algorithm, the concentration-based convergence theory, and then empirical results on classic control and MuJoCo. The experimental setup note is isolated.
